title: Federal Reserve Board announces final individual capital requirements for large banks, effective on October 1
summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced final individual capital requirements for large banks on August 29, 2025, effective October 1. These requirements are based on stress test results and consist of a minimum 4.5% CET1 requirement, a stress capital buffer of at least 2.5%, and applicable surcharges for the largest complex banks. Banks whose capital falls below their announced requirement face automatic restrictions on capital distributions and bonus payments. The announcement follows a Board proposal in April 2025 to average stress test results over two consecutive years to reduce volatility.
key_points: Each bank's CET1 capital requirement consists of: 4.5% minimum (same for all banks), stress capital buffer (at least 2.5% based on stress test results), and capital surcharge for largest/most complex banks updated annually in Q1
If a bank's capital falls below its total requirement, automatic restrictions apply on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments
Morgan Stanley's capital requirement was not included as the firm requested reconsideration to reduce its stress capital buffer; final requirement expected by September 30, 2025
The Board proposed in April 2025 to average stress test results over two consecutive years to reduce year-over-year volatility in capital requirements
Requirements represent a period of transition pending finalization of the averaging rule proposed in April 2025
why_it_matters: These capital requirements directly affect large banks' regulatory capital planning and risk management. The stress capital buffer framework ensures banks maintain sufficient capital to absorb shocks in adverse scenarios. Banks below requirements face automatic distribution restrictions, creating clear incentives for capital adequacy. The proposed averaging rule, if finalized, would smooth capital requirement volatility, reducing unexpected swings in regulatory capital needs year-over-year.
market_structure_context: This announcement establishes the regulatory capital framework for large banks under the Federal Reserve's stress testing regime (DFAST). The structure includes automatic capital distribution restrictions for non-compliance, making it binding regulatory requirements rather than guidance. The proposed two-year averaging of stress test results represents a potential modification to the existing stress testing methodology that would affect how capital buffers are calculated.
